observed.consequential_claim: The journal is append-preserving: no method updates or deletes a journal row, retraction appends a counter-record and leaves the original intact, and a rewritten history stops verifying rather than quietly replacing the real one.
observed.observer_independence_basis: This session did not build services/record and did not edit it. Git authorship cannot establish builder identity here - every commit in this repository carries Bdo's identity, including those a model session authored - so independence rests on the reachable facts instead: the observation drives the service only as a subprocess through the CLI declared in services/record/contracts/service.json, never imports soveraeign_record_service, and recomputes the digest chain from the rule written in services/record/CHARTER.md rather than from core.py. The pre-existing walker scripts/witness_record.py was deliberately not read or run before the probe was written, so the two are not a common-source pair.
observed.note_on_core_py: core.py is listed as read state because its bytes were digested for this receipt. Its contents were not read while the probe's digest recomputation was written; that rule was taken from CHARTER.md alone.

chain_rule_is_the_declared_one.detail: All four seeded entries' stored digests were reproduced exactly by recomputing sha256 over prev_digest|kind|subject|actor|canonical-payload from the rule stated in CHARTER.md. An outside reader can verify this journal from the documentation without the implementation.

no_mutation_on_the_reachable_surface.detail: The declared surface offers 11 operations and none of them is an UPDATE or DELETE against a journal entry, receipt, counter-record, or the digest chain.

payload_rewrite_is_caught.detail: A payload rewritten directly in SQLite, behind the CLI, makes reconstruct-journal refuse with DIGEST_MISMATCH at exit 2.

entry_removal_is_caught.detail: A journal row deleted from the middle directly in SQLite makes reconstruct-journal refuse with DIGEST_MISMATCH at exit 2.

retraction_preserves_the_original.detail: After counter-entry, the original entry is still readable through read-entry with its payload and its digest unchanged, and the chain still verifies.

projection_is_rebuildable.detail: read-projection refuses with MISSING_PRECONDITION until a projection is built, rebuild-projections reproduces a byte-identical row after every projection is dropped, the journal head is unchanged across the cycle, and every projection read declares authoritative=false.

design_record_refused.detail: An entry sourced from SPEC.md, CONTRACT.md, STATUS.yaml, or AGENTS.md is refused with DESIGN_RECORD_REFUSED at exit 2. The design and operational Systems of Record do not merge through this door.

export_of_a_broken_journal_refused.detail: With a payload rewritten in SQLite, export-journal refuses and writes no file. A broken chain is not copied.

restore_into_non_empty_refused.detail: restore-journal into a store that already holds entries refuses with MISSING_PRECONDITION at exit 2.

truncation_admission_is_accurate.detail: An export truncated by one entry, with both self-declared fields (head_digest and entry_count) rewritten to match the shorter document, verifies clean at exit 0 with no external head and is refused at exit 2 when the true head is supplied via --expect-head. The charter states this limitation exactly and does not overstate the guarantee.

history_cannot_be_quietly_rewritten.detail: Three stored columns sit outside the declared digest rule: entry_id, source_address, and recorded_at. Rewriting all three in SQLite leaves reconstruct-journal at exit 0. Escalated: inverting every entry's recorded_at so the journal reports the reverse chronological order, and rewriting every source_address to a fabricated lineage path, left the replay at exit 0 with a byte-identical head digest. The chain does exactly what the chain rule says; the charter sentence 'a rewritten history stops verifying rather than quietly replacing the real one' covers less of an entry than it reads as covering.
history_cannot_be_quietly_rewritten.governing_rule: AGENTS.md, State and execution: every consequential decision emits an attributable event with actor, operation, reason, timestamp, exact input addresses/digests. Timestamp and input address are two of the three fields outside the chain.
history_cannot_be_quietly_rewritten.what_would_discharge_it: Either extend the digest rule to cover recorded_at, source_address, and entry_id and restate it in CHARTER.md, or narrow the charter sentence to name the covered fields and record the consequence of leaving the rest uncovered. Both are repairs, and a witness may not make either.
